newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso unlikely to plunge much further.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso unlikely to plunge much further.

text.p: The Philippine peso depreciation is likely to settle at around 10 to 15 percent after it has recovered from the jolt of Friday's effective devaluation, Economic Planning Secretary Cielito Habito said.

Initial analysis by the policy-making National Economic Development Authority (NEDA) showed inflation could be held to single-digit levels after the Central Bank's decision to allow the peso to trade within a wider range, Habito said in a statement on Sunday.

"Once the initial knee-jerk reactions in the market subside, equilibrium will likely be restored at a level representing not more than 10-15 percent depreciation," he said. The peso tumbled 11.5 percent to 29.40 pesos to the dollar after the central bank allowed the market to find the rate.
Habito said there was no reason for the exchange rate to spiral because the Philippines' economic fundamentals remained sound while the productive sectors enjoyed robust growth rates.
"Our initial calculations show that a one-peso increase in the peso-dollar exchange rate will add less than one percentage point to the full year annual inflation rate," Habito said.
Before Friday's peso plunge, the government had set the inflation target for this year at between 5.2 and 5.7 percent.
Habito said "things could have turned for the worse" had the government continued to defend the peso against speculative attacks.
"It is in fact a good time to have a much-needed depreciation, because the inflation rate is very low at less than five percent," he added.
